newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Dickson proposes bid for U.S. Barney's.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Dickson proposes bid for U.S. Barney's.

text.p: Hong Kong-based upmarket retailer Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd said it submitted a proposal on Friday to acquire United States luxury retailer Barney's Inc.
The proposal offers existing Barney's owners US$240 million in cash and a minority interest in Barney's future non-U.S. store licensing income.
"Barney's represents a unique opportunity for the group to establish a meaningful business presence in the United States," Dickson's chairman, Dickson Poon, told a news conference.
Barney's, one of the leading retailers of mens' and womens' apparel in the United States, reported total sales of US$366 million for the 53 weeks to August 3, 1996.
Barney's has been operating in bankruptcy for more than a year. It said on January 24 it had received an extension until May 5 from a U.S. bankruptcy court judge to file a reorganisation plan.
Dickson has a worldwide retail network of over 270 outlets.
"We firmly believe that we have enough experience and talents to turn within a short time Barney's financial position into something that is of good contribution to Dickson," Poon said.
He said the group would be able to fund the deal.

"At this stage, a rights issue or fundraising are totally out of my mind," he said. "The group currently has sufficient cash reserves and banking facilities available to satisfy this consideration in full.
"Our cash position is approxminately HK$1.3 billion (US$168 million)," he said. He did not give details of the funding plan.
Analysts were mixed about Dickson's proposal.

"Our view on the news is positive, since Dickson has a good track record in turning around loss-making companies and the brand of Barney's is not bad and there is a good chance that they can also be successful this time," a European house analyst said.
Another said the acquisition would raise Dickson's gearing. "There is quite a bit of debt still outstanding in the Barney's operation that hasn't been paid.
"It's a different operation for them... It's going to be a challenge for them but obviously they (have taken) challenge in the past."

An analyst at a local brokerage house said: "The price looked a bit under the market's expectation of between US$300-$400 million but information available is so little at the moment, people cannot make fair judgment."
Poon said the offer of minority interest in the future non-U.S. store licensing income made the Barney's bid more attractive, but he did not specify its value.
He said the group would continue to examine its earnings capabilities and would remain financially strong for further investment opportunities.
"There are different investment opportunities that the group is examining in addition to Barney's," he said, giving no details.
The takeover might not materialise because it would need the approval of the U.S. bankruptcy court and other bidders might submit competing proposals, he said.
He expected it could take between four and eight months for Dickson to secure required approvals for the acquisition.
